title: Pointwise smoothness from a smooth fibre
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], let $x\in X$ and $s=f(x)$. Assume the local ring map $\mathcal O_{S,s}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Then $f$ is smooth at $x$ (there is an open neighbourhood of $x$ on which $f$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]) if and only if the fibre morphism $X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-weil-residue-field] is smooth at the point corresponding to $x$.

proof.text: Suppose $f$ is smooth on an open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$. Apply [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion] to $f|_U:U\to S$: its fibre $U_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is smooth. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product], $U_s$ identifies with the open subscheme of $X_s$ lying above $U$, compatibly with the morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$. This open contains the point corresponding to $x$ by [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. It is therefore the required smooth neighbourhood in the fibre.

Conversely suppose $X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is smooth at $x$. By [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] choose affine neighbourhoods $W=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$ of $x$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$ of $s$, with $f(W)\subset V$ and $A$ finitely presented over $R$. Write $\varphi:R\to A$ for the induced map and $\mathfrak q\subset A$ for $x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-induced-ring-map-spec-square], $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ represents $s$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-stalk-localization], the local map $R_{\mathfrak p}\to A_{\mathfrak q}$ is the given stalk map under ring isomorphisms. It is flat by hypothesis; no flatness away from $x$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 01V9, lemma-smooth-at-point, affine reduction for (2) implies (1); Algebra Tag 00TF hypotheses (1) and (2)

proof.text: Put $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $F=A\otimes_R k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-residue-field-identification], $k\cong\kappa(s)$ compatibly with the maps to $S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product], $\operatorname{Spec}F$ is the open subscheme of $X_s$ above $W$, over $k$. The point over $x$ is $\mathfrak Q=\ker(F\to\kappa(\mathfrak q))$, $a\otimes\lambda\mapsto\bar a\bar\lambda$: its contraction is $\mathfrak q$, so [def-pc-scheme-fibre] identifies it with the unique point over $x$. Let $N\subset X_s$ be a smooth neighbourhood of this point. There is $h\in F\setminus\mathfrak Q$ with $D(h)\subset N\cap\operatorname{Spec}F$: the complement of this open in $\operatorname{Spec}F$ is $V(I)$ for an ideal $I$, and $\mathfrak Q\notin V(I)$ gives $h\in I\setminus\mathfrak Q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], $D(h)=\operatorname{Spec}F_h$. Its inclusion into $N$ is an open immersion, so [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition] makes $\operatorname{Spec}F_h\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ smooth. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine], $k\to F_h$ is a smooth ring map. Thus $k\to F$ is smooth at $\mathfrak Q$ by [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal].

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-smooth-fibre-smooth-at-prime] to $\varphi:R\to A$, $\mathfrak p$, and $\mathfrak q$. Its finite-presentation condition holds with the element $1\notin\mathfrak q$ because $A$ is finitely presented over $R$ (step 2). Its local-flatness condition is step 2, and its smooth-fibre condition is step 3, with precisely the kernel prime $\mathfrak Q$ specified in its statement. It follows that $R\to A$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q$. Unpacking [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal], choose $g\in A\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that $R\to A_g$ is a smooth ring map.

source.place: Tag 01V9, lemma-smooth-at-point, (2) implies (1) by Algebra Tag 00TF, lemma-flat-fibre-smooth

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], $\operatorname{Spec}A_g$ is the open neighbourhood $W_g=D(g)$ of $x$ in $W$. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine], $W_g\to V$ is smooth. Its composite $W_g\to S$ is locally of finite presentation: each affine finite-presentation neighbourhood over the open $V$ is also such a neighbourhood over $S$, by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. To check formal smoothness, take a first order thickening $T\subset T'$ of affine $S$-schemes and a map $T\to W_g$ over $S$. By [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], $T$ and $T'$ have the same underlying points. The structure map $T'\to S$ therefore lands in $V$ since its restriction to $T$ does, and factors uniquely through $V$ by [def-weil-open-immersion]. The square is now over $V$; formal smoothness of $W_g\to V$ gives a lift $T'\to W_g$ by [def-sbc-formally-smooth], which is also a lift over $S$. Thus $W_g\to S$ is smooth by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Since $x\in W_g$, this is the required smooth neighbourhood of $x$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NW-b517b12f2 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Stacks 01V9 (lemma-smooth-at-point), statement and full proof, with Algebra 00TF (lemma-flat-fibre-smooth) and Definition 00TB. The item is 01V9 (1)<=>(2) with local flatness moved into the hypotheses: equivalent to the source, nothing added or weakened, and its only citer (lem-trf-generic-fibre-points-smooth) uses it in that form. Step 1 (forward): sbc-lem-smooth-criterion is applied to f|_U; that node is closed in slopmaster2, so it is a closed tool. The open-fibre-product lemma identifies U_s with p^{-1}(U) in X_s, and the fibre definition puts the point over x in it. Step 2: the lfp chart plus the spec-square and stalk-localization nodes make the stalk map R_p->A_q, flat only at q. Step 3: kappa(s)=kappa(p) via the residue-field identification; Spec(A tensor_R k) is an open of X_s via 01JR/01I4; Q=ker(F->kappa(q)) contracts to q. The D(h) Zariski argument is correct and elementary; open immersion into smooth N, then 02H6, gives k->F_h smooth, so k->F is smooth at Q. Step 4: the 00TF node applies with g=1, step-2 flatness and step-3 fibre smoothness; it uses the fibre A tensor_R kappa(p), not A/pA. Step 5: D(g) is an open neighbourhood of x and smooth over V; the step proves that composing with the open V in S keeps smoothness (lfp, plus thickenings have the same points so T'->S factors through V), which is correct since the cited composition lemma has the other order. Edge cases: non-flat Spec k->Spec k[t] is excluded by the hypothesis; F_p(t^{1/p})/F_p(t) and the node of uv=0 are false on both sides; empty X is vacuous. No new nodes. rg for 01V9/lemma-smooth-at-point finds only the differential criterion, global criteria and the Fitting locus, none a duplicate. Mathlib IsSmoothAt.of_formallySmooth_fiber needs the whole fibre smooth and Smooth.of_smooth_fiberToSpecResidueField is global, so neither is a leaf.
